figure: Figure 3 of the method page, method/figures/floor-light.svg and floor-dark.svg, drawn by method/figures/floor.py from method/figures/data/floor.json

example.what: QUASR 954 at 4.5 times the toroidal flux its file asks for: a surface outside the design's own boundary, verified
example.why: HSX at 0.0359221439332229 Wb, the surface of the other figures, refines in two levels (112, 48 at 1.3e-9, then 192, 96 at 3.0e-15), and so does QUASR 954 at its own request (24, 24 at 1.9e-11, then 48, 32 at 1.1e-15), each solved separately by the same torux.solve. At 4.5 times its request QUASR 954 refines in three, spread down the spectrum.

surface.a1_is: the largest sqrt(R_mn^2 + Z_mn^2) with m >= 1, reached at m = 1: the spectrum is drawn relative to it

spectrum.what: for each m the largest sqrt(R_mn^2 + Z_mn^2) over n, relative to a1: the heavy curve, m = 1 to M
spectrum.spikes_are: the harmonics nearest resonance, where m iota is closest to a multiple n N_fp of N_fp: every N_fp / |iota| = 24.4 in m

n_side.what: the same over m, for each |n|: not drawn

refinement.bn_is: the largest |B.n|/|B| the solver measured at that level on a grid shifted half a cell from the one it solved on: the circles

prediction_rule.rule: torux.family.predict_resolution fits a straight line to the log of the spectrum over its last half. The next M is where that line meets floor, plus 2, at most maxfac times the current M, raised to the next value of torux.family.LADDER. N likewise. The dashed line is the first of these fits, drawn from m = fit_m[0] to meets_floor_at_m

floor.source: results/evaluator/test_output.txt: the largest |B.n|/|B| that the independent evaluator, in extended precision, reads on an exact invariant torus written as a double-precision series. results/README.md rounds it to 3.9e-16
